# Connect the cfo.ai MCP server
Source: https://docs.cfo.ai/integrations/mcp-server

Connect Claude Code, Codex, or another MCP client to cfo.ai, authorize access, and choose the correct workspace.

cfo.ai runs its own MCP server at `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`. Any AI client that supports remote MCP servers can connect, including Claude Code and Codex.

The connection lets an external agent use the same workspace tools Ari uses. Those tools can inspect your Model and, when authorized, change live Pages, Scenarios, Variables, Dimensions, and formulas.

You, Ari, and the external agent share the same Model. Work created through the connection remains visible in your cfo.ai workspace, where you can inspect the assumptions, edit the result, or continue the work with Ari.

Setup below covers Claude Code and Codex.

## Before you start

You need a cfo.ai account with access to the intended workspace. If you do not have one yet, sign up at [app.cfo.ai](https://app.cfo.ai) and complete the required account setup first.

## Claude Code

<Steps>
  <Step title="Add the MCP server">
    Open a terminal and add cfo.ai as an MCP server:

    ```bash theme={null}
    claude mcp add --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Start Claude Code">
    ```bash theme={null}
    claude
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Open the MCP menu">
    Type `/mcp` and look for `cfoai` in the list of servers.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Authenticate">
    Select `cfoai`, then choose **Authenticate**. A browser window opens. Make sure you're logged into your cfo.ai account before approving the connection.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Codex

<Steps>
  <Step title="Add the MCP server">
    Open a terminal and add cfo.ai as an MCP server:

    ```bash theme={null}
    codex mcp add cfoai --url https://api.cfo.ai/mcp
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Authenticate">
    ```bash theme={null}
    codex mcp login cfoai
    ```

    A browser window opens. Make sure you're logged into your cfo.ai account before approving the connection.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Verify">
    Start Codex with `codex`, then type `/mcp` to confirm `cfoai` is connected.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Other MCP clients

Any harness that supports remote MCP servers can connect. Add `https://api.cfo.ai/mcp` as a custom connector or MCP server in your agent's settings, then sign in with your cfo.ai account when the browser prompt appears.

## Choose the correct workspace

If your account belongs to one workspace, the connection can use it automatically. If your account belongs to several workspaces, ask the agent to call `list_orgs`, select the correct workspace by its ID or slug, and pass that value as `org_id` on each later tool call.

Writes apply to the selected live workspace. Use a Scenario when you want an external agent to work on an alternative plan without changing Main.

## What the connection exposes

The server publishes Ari's public workspace tools, such as `inspect_table_blocks`,

content.content:
Focus areas Planning Break a goal into actionable steps. Tool use Choose tools, supply inputs and handle responses. State Retain state across steps, runs and failures. Context Bring in relevant information; leave out the rest. Execution Keep long tasks running to completion. Recovery Handle failures and unexpected results. Verification Check that results are correct. Iteration Use each result to choose the next step. See example tasks These examples show the size of task we have in mind. They aren't separate tracks, and you don't have to build one of them. Fix a GitHub issue An agent investigates a GitHub issue, writes and tests a fix, and proposes the fix. Answer a research question with sources An agent splits a question into smaller questions and gathers evidence for each one. When sources disagree, the agent works out which source to trust and writes an answer with citations. Watch a running system An agent watches a running system for unusual behavior. When the agent finds a problem, it looks for the cause and takes an action to fix it. Several agents working together Several worker agents each solve part of a task on their own. A coordinator agent then combines their results and settles any disagreements. Work while things change An agent works on a long task while the environment it works in keeps changing. Requirements Use , and Your project must use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. Use neatlogs and Entire to build and improve your agent, and cfo.ai to plan its business. neatlogs Works with any agent Trace every agent run Find the code behind a failure, then compare runs to verify your fix. Model and tool calls, inputs and responses State changes, retries, failures and agent messages Latency, token usage and cost neatlogs / traces Example run Research agent Every step, in context. Success Span tree Duration agent research_agent 2.84s llm plan 620ms tool search_documents 480ms llm compose_answer 1.42s tool verify_citations 320ms 5 spans 1.8k tokens $0.003 Entire For coding agents Give your coding agent repository context Open-source tools for understanding your codebase and the history of AI-made changes. Checkpoints: save the context behind each change entire-graph: map relationships across your repository agent-workspace Example PR Preserve state across retries #42 agent/recovery → main Conversation 2 Files changed 1 +3 −1 src/agent/run.ts − const state = createState(); + const state = checkpoint.restore(); + await agent.run(state); + checkpoint.save(state); Checkpoint attached Context, decisions & changes cfo.ai Plan the business with cfo.ai Use cfo.ai to plan your agent’s pricing, costs, revenue and runway. Include the resulting business plan in your submission. neatHack signup & credits Sign up at cfo.ai/neathacks ↗ A card is required during signup. Immediately after signing up, cancel your subscription in Settings → Billing. You won’t be billed if you cancel immediately. The neatHack team will provide your cfo.ai credits directly. cfo.ai / agent economics Example model C6 ƒx =(C3-C4)/C3 Illustrative monthly economics for two scenarios A B C 1 Monthly model Base Growth 2 Customers 100 250 3 Revenue $2,000 $5,000 4 Infra + inference $400 $850 5 Gross profit $1,600 $4,150 6 Gross margin 80% 83% Unit economics Runway Scenarios Judging criteria Judges score each project in five categories. Each category is scored out of 100, and the categories are weighted as shown to give a final score out of 100. The agent How well the agent, or the system of agents, handles a substantial task from start to finish. 30 % Use of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai How effectively you used neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai to build, improve and plan a business around the agent. 25 % Demo video How clearly the demo video explains the agent and your use of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. 20 % Building in public How you shared your project with other people while you built it. 15 % Usefulness and originality Whether the agent solves a problem that people have, in a new way. 10 % Evidence & verification Back up each claim in your submission with evidence that judges can check. The agent improved A run before your change and a run after it, e.g., two neatlogs traces, with the numbers you compared You used neatlogs Links to neatlogs traces from your project, or screenshots of them You used Entire Checkpoints or entire-graph output from your repository You used cfo.ai A business plan covering your agent’s pricing, costs, revenue and runway The agent recovers from failures A run where an action failed, showing what the agent did next You built in public Links to what you shared during the hackathon, tagged #neatHack You wrote the code during the hackathon A public repository with commits dated during the hackathon Schedule Build October 10–12, submit October 12. Winners are announced October 16. All times below are in IST. October 10 Day 1 9:00 AM IST — Kickoff call We’ll kick things off with TheVibeFounder , a surprise workshop (more on this later tonight), and a Q&A before everyone starts building. The kickoff call is at 9:00 AM IST on October 10. Submissions open October 12 at 7:00 PM IST, with a planned close around 11:55 PM IST. The final cutoff will be announced on Discord. Winners are announced on October 16. Can I build with a team? Come solo or in a team of 1–4 people. Every member must register on Luma using the same team name, and each person can join only one team. What can I build beforehand? You can plan your idea in advance, but all code must be written between the start on October 10 and the deadline on October 12. Finished or half-built projects cannot be brought into the event. Use neatlogs throughout development to capture traces, investigate failures, identify bottlenecks and improve your agent. How many tracks are there? There is one track, Build an agent that works (literally), and every project competes for the same prizes. You can build a single agent or a system of several agents. The example tasks are ideas, not separate tracks. Do I have to use a partner technology? Yes. Every project must use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, with a clear role for each in building the agent or planning its business. Your demo must cover all three tools. What do I need to submit? Each team submits one project as a public quote post of the official neatlogs submission post on X before the confirmed cutoff. Use Submit on X to open the draft, fill in your team, name, project, public repository and demo link, keep the official post attached, then publish on X. Include supporting evidence in your repository. Include a demo video of three minutes or less and a public code repository. The video must explicitly cover neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai: architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result for each tool. Judges must be able to verify that commits were made during the hackathon. Submissions open October 12 at 7:00 PM IST, with a planned close around 11:55 PM IST. Submit any time during this window; the final cutoff will be announced on Discord. Entries after the confirmed cutoff will not be judged. The Submit on X button appears once the window and official post are live. Opening the draft alone does not submit your project. neatlogs and cfo.ai will engage with the first 50 quote tweets. How are projects judged? Mentors score each project using the published criteria. The agent is worth 30% of the final score, the use of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai is worth 25%, and the demo video is worth 20%. Building in public is worth 15%, and usefulness and originality are worth 10%. The judges' decision is final, and the community winner is judged separately. How does the community winner work? The community winner goes to the project that generates the strongest genuine community interest during the hackathon. We look at the quality and creativity of the product and demo, the quality of the launch and content, shares and discussion, genuine engagement, and whether people are excited enough to try, share or talk about it. Existing audience size or follower count does not decide the winner. The project must use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, but partner usage is not part of community winner scoring. Bought likes or bot activity will disqualify a team. What are the conduct rules? Be respectful in Discord and all event spaces. ######## https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill
rd it as pending; never invent eligibility, judging weights, prizes, deadlines or submission links. Every project must use neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai. Record how each tool is used and collect evidence for all three. Show how neatlogs and Entire support the agent, and use cfo.ai to plan its pricing, costs, revenue and runway. Include the business plan in the submission and explain all three tools in the demo. Maintain hackathon.md at the project root. Preserve existing entries. Start with: - Project: name, one-sentence purpose and the problem it addresses - Team: only names/handles the builder chooses to publish - Stack: actual services and integrations used - Build log: dated changes, experiments, failures, fixes and evidence - Demo: URL and instructions, when available - Known limitations and next steps - Submission: confirmed requirements and any outstanding items After each work session, inspect the changes and ask about decisions you cannot infer. Append a concise dated entry. Distinguish planned work from completed work. Record tests that actually ran and failures that remain. Link to sanitized, shareable evidence only. Never include API keys, .env contents, personal data, private traces, access tokens or customer information. Do not fabricate results. Before a demo, summarize what works and how to reproduce it. Check the latest published requirements with the builder. Never register, publish, deploy or submit on their behalf without their instruction. This skill does not establish contest rules and does not automatically qualify a project.

e your first call Save your key privately Set LITELLM_API_KEY in your backend’s process environment. If you use a .env file, load it in your app and exclude it from Git. Point your client here API base URL Copy API base URL https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1 Use your key as the Bearer token. With Python, install openai and use the example below. Choose a model nova-micro nova-lite nova-pro nova-2-lite claude-haiku claude-sonnet-4.6 claude-opus-4.6 Python Copy Python import os from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI( base_url="https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1", api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_API_KEY"], ) response = client.chat.completions.create( model="claude-haiku", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], ) print(response.choices[0].message.content) cURL example & model list cURL Copy cURL curl https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"claude-haiku","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello!"}]}' List models Copy List models curl https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_API_KEY" One key. One shared allowance. The provider sets a $ 20 budget per key over 30 days. Requests stop when that budget is used. All teammates share it. This is separate from the $25 AWS infrastructure allowance. It doesn’t add Bedrock permissions to your AWS account.

<Note>
  `entire enable` creates `.entire/settings.json` and `.entire/.gitignore` so collaborators share project settings. Entire keeps `.entire/settings.local.json` local for personal overrides.
</Note>

## 3. Create Your First Checkpoint

<iframe title="How to Create Your First Checkpoint" />

Start your agent from the repository root and give it a small task:

```text theme={null}
Create a file named hello-entire.md with a short note explaining that this is my first Entire checkpoint.
```

When the agent finishes, commit the change:

```bash theme={null}
git add hello-entire.md
git commit -m "Add first Entire checkpoint"
```

Entire asks whether to link the commit to the agent session:

```text theme={null}
Entire: Active <agent> session detected

Link this commit to session context?
  [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways (remember my choice):
```

Press `Enter` or type `y`.

You have created a checkpoint. It links the commit to the prompt, transcript, tool calls, and files from the agent session.

View it with:

```bash theme={null}
entire checkpoint list
```

<Note>
  Choose `always` at the commit prompt if you want Entire to link future agent-assisted commits automatically.
</Note>

Checkpoint storage depends on the repository configuration. See [Session Storage](/guides/checkpoints/checkpoint-storage) for storage and push behavior.

## 4. Mirror Your Repository

<iframe title="How to Mirror Your Repository" />

A mirror lets agents clone and pull through Entire while GitHub remains the upstream repository.

Log in before you begin:

```bash theme={null}
entire login
```

Also make sure the [Entire GitHub App](/guides/repositories/github-app-access) can access the repository. An organization admin may need to approve the app.

Create a mirror:

```bash theme={null}
entire repo mirror add
```

Choose your repository and the region where you want Entire to host it. Choose a region close to your agents or one that meets your organization's data-residency requirements.

Then add the mirror as a remote in this checkout:

```bash theme={null}
entire repo remote add entire
```

Check the result:

```bash theme={null}
git remote -v
```

There should now be an `entire` remote on an `entire://` URL, with `origin` still pointing at GitHub. Fetch and push through it:

```bash theme={null}
git fetch entire
git push entire
```

Entire sends pushes through the mirror to GitHub. Your existing GitHub access, branch protection, and review rules still apply.

<Note>
  To send everyday Git commands through Entire without naming a remote, point `origin` at the mirror instead:

  ```bash theme={null}
  entire repo remote add origin --override
  ```

  `--override` is required because `origin` already exists. Entire prints the URL it replaces, and that printout is the only record of it, so copy it somewhere first if you want to restore it later.
</Note>

<span />

## Optional: Create a New Repository on Entire

<iframe title="Create an Entire repository on entire.io" />

You can now host your code on Entire.

A project holds your repositories. Create a project, replacing `readme` with an available project name and `nodo` with your organization's name:

```bash theme={null}
entire project create readme --owner nodo
```

If you already have a project, use its name in the next command. Create a repository replacing the name `documentation` in the project:

## neatHack brief: neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai (checked against docs, Oct 11 2026)

**First, a correction to memory.** Xcode Command Line Tools are now installed on this Mac. `/usr/bin/git` reports 2.50.1. There is still no brew. Entire depends hard on git (≥2.25, and ≥2.36 for entire-graph). It uses git hooks, and checkpoints go to the remote through the **pre-push hook**. So you must push with `git push`; pushing through `gh api` skips the hook and the checkpoints never reach GitHub.

### Rules that affect the build (https://neatlogs.com/hackathon)
- **Judging weights:** agent 30%, use of the 3 tools 25%, demo video (≤3 min, must cover each tool's architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result) 20%, building in public (#neatHack) 15%, usefulness/originality 10%.
- **Evidence the judges ask for:**
  - before and after neatlogs traces, with the numbers you compared
  - trace links or screenshots
  - Entire Checkpoints or entire-graph output
  - cfo.ai plan covering pricing, costs, revenue and runway
  - a run that shows recovery from a failure
  - public repo with commits made during the event
- **How to submit:** quote-post the official neatlogs post on X, Oct 12, 7:00–11:55 PM IST. The final cutoff is announced on Discord.
- **Free models:** a LiteLLM key, OpenAI-compatible, base `https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1`. Models: nova-micro/lite/pro, nova-2-lite, claude-haiku, claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-opus-4.6. $20 per team (https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/models).
- **Hackathon skill** (https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill): asks you to keep a `hackathon.md` at the repo root (project, stack, dated build log, evidence, limitations).

### 1. neatlogs
- **Docs:** full text at https://docs.neatlogs.com/llms-full.txt. SDKs: Python, TypeScript (Node ≥18), Go, Browser, plus HTTP `POST /v1/trace` and OTLP/gRPC `ingest.neatlogs.com:443` with header `x-api-key`.
- **TypeScript install:** `npm install neatlogs@latest`. The wizard is `npx @neatlogs/wizard@latest`.
- **Basic trace:**
```ts
import { init, wrapOpenAI, span, flush, shutdown } from 'neatlogs';
await init({ apiKey: process.env.NEATLOGS_API_KEY, workflowName: 'my-agent' });
const client = wrapOpenAI(new OpenAI({ baseURL: LITELLM_BASE, apiKey: process.env.LITELLM_API_KEY }));
const run = span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW' }, async (goal) => {...});
const tool = span({ kind: 'TOOL', toolName: 'search' }, async (q) => {...});
await flush(); await shutdown();   // short scripts lose traces without this
```
  - `init()` is async.
  - Wrap the entry point in a `WORKFLOW` span so all calls land in one trace.
  - Using `wrapOpenAI` with a custom `baseURL` (for LiteLLM) is my assumption; the docs don't show that case.
- **Explicit wrappers (TypeScript has no auto-instrumentation):**
  - `wrapAnthropic`
  - `wrapAISDK(ai)` from `neatlogs/ai` (AI SDK v6/v7; v7 needs Node 22+)
  - `wrapClaudeAgentSDK` from `neatlogs/claude-agent-sdk`
  - `wrapMastra`
  - `openaiAgentsProcessor()`
  - `langchainHandler()`
  - Python additionally has `neatlogs.wrap(...)` and LiteLLM support (`pip install "neatlogs[litellm]"`).
- **Sessions:** `identify({ sessionId, endUserId }, fn)`.
- **Claude Code tracing:** `npm i -g @neatlogs/claude-code && neatlogs-claude-code setup --global --api-key KEY`. This registers hooks and turns each Claude Code session into a trace.
- **MCP:** yes, Claude Code can read traces. Run `npx @neatlogs/wizard mcp --api-key KEY`, or add this to `.mcp.json`: `{"neatlogs":{"type":"http","url":"https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer KEY"}}}`.
  - Tools: `search_traces`, `get_trace_context`, `list_detections`, `get_detection_trend`, `triage_*` (fixes and investigations), `log_trace`, `whoami`.
- **Product features:** Investigate (Neat AI, Fast and Pro modes), Detections, Fixes, Evals (human or AI judges), Experiments (prompt versions plus Playground). The Datasets part of Experiments is "coming soon".
- **Not verified:** how to make a trace link public. The Public API has `GET /api/v1/public/traces/{id}/sharing` and the CLI has `neatlogs sharing traces get`, but I found no documented public-link toggle. Plan on screenshots plus dashboard URLs, and ask on Discord.
- **"Compare runs":** no dedicated docs page. The local tool neatroots (github.com/neatlogs/neatroots) offers "compare runs" through MCP.
- **Free tier:** 100k spans a month (hard cap), 3 investigations a month, 5 detectors, 2 users, 1 project, 14-day retention. Winners get 3 months of Pro.

### 2. Entire (https://docs.entire.io/llms-full.txt)
- **What it is:** Git hosting plus agent session capture. It was founded by the former GitHub CEO. The CLI is open source (MIT) at github.com/entireio/cli, latest v0.11.4, with darwin arm64 and amd64 builds.
- **Install without brew:** `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`. I read the script; it supports darwin and installs `entire` and `git-remote-entire` into `~/.local/bin`.
- **Setup in the repo:** `entire enable -y --agent claude-code`. This writes Claude Code hooks to `.claude/settings.json` and creates `.entire/settings.json`.
- **How a checkpoint is made:** on commit, Entire asks "Link this commit to session context? [Y/n/a]". Answer `a` (always) so Claude-made commits link automatically. The commit then gets an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer, and the transcript, tool calls, tokens, subagents and attribution are stored.
- **Storage:**
  - Default since 0.10.0 is ref-based: `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<ULID>`. GitHub's UI does not show these refs.
  - The branch backend stores everything on `entire/checkpoints/v1` with 12-hex IDs.
- **Use the branch backend:** `entire enable --checkpoint-backend branch` (or `entire configure --checkpoint-backend branch`).
  - **The judges' tool expects it:** entireio/entire-judge `add` fetches only `refs/heads/entire/*`, and its trailer regex matches only 12-hex IDs.
  - **Caveat:** I didn't confirm whether its `brain refresh` step fetches ref-based checkpoints on its own.
  - The branch is also visible on GitHub, and checkpoints show at `https://entire.io/gh/<org>/<repo>/commit/<sha>`. That view may need `entire login` plus the GitHub App.
- **entire-graph:** a plugin that maps code relationships for agents (claims up to 71% token savings).
  - Install with `entire plugin install graph`, check with `entire graph version`.
  - Run `entire graph init-agents --repo .`. This writes `.entire/graph-agent.md` and a managed block in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. Commit them.
  - Then prompt the agent, for example "Use entire-graph to find…". Needs git ≥2.36.
  - Also available: `entire mcp` (stdio MCP server), Brain, Search, Dispatches (shareable markdown summary of agent work).
- **Judge tool (github.com/entireio/entire-judge):** worth designing around. It scores:
  - authenticity (whether sessions began after the event started)
  - prompting_skill
  - idea/plan/execution (uses entire-graph data if present)
  - integrity (red flag when the team ignored warnings from the coding agent)
  - effort_consistency (rewards multiple sessions over one burst)
  - cli_awareness (rewards using `entire graph`, `entire brain` and Entire skills inside sessions)
- **Kickoff advice from Entire's judge:** "simple but elegant", and use Entire well. A previous winner built an Obsidian-style visual on entire-graph. PRs to Entire are a nice-to-have.

### 3. cfo.ai
- **What it is:** "Ari", an AI CFO. It builds a live financial model (Pages, Tables, Variables, Scenarios) from your data or from chat. Price: $500/mo after a 14-day trial.
- **Hackathon signup:** at cfo.ai/neathacks a card is required; cancel right away in Settings → Billing. The neatHack team supplies credits. The user has to do this step.
- **Outputs:**
  - Share → External link: read-only, no sign-in needed, optional password, choose which Scenario it shows. One link can cover several Pages. This is the judge link.
  - "Download spreadsheet" on any Page with tables (xlsx with live formulas). Ari can also export several Pages into one workbook.
- **MCP (verified):** `claude mcp add --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`, then `/mcp` → Authenticate in the browser.

## neatHack brief: neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai (checked against docs, Oct 11 2026)

**First, a correction to memory.** Xcode Command Line Tools are now installed on this Mac. `/usr/bin/git` reports 2.50.1. There is still no brew. Entire depends hard on git (≥2.25, and ≥2.36 for entire-graph). It uses git hooks, and checkpoints go to the remote through the **pre-push hook**. So you must push with `git push`; pushing through `gh api` skips the hook and the checkpoints never reach GitHub.

### Rules that affect the build (https://neatlogs.com/hackathon)
- **Judging weights:** agent 30%, use of the 3 tools 25%, demo video (≤3 min, must cover each tool's architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result) 20%, building in public (#neatHack) 15%, usefulness/originality 10%.
- **Evidence the judges ask for:**
  - before and after neatlogs traces, with the numbers you compared
  - trace links or screenshots
  - Entire Checkpoints or entire-graph output
  - cfo.ai plan covering pricing, costs, revenue and runway
  - a run that shows recovery from a failure
  - public repo with commits made during the event
- **How to submit:** quote-post the official neatlogs post on X, Oct 12, 7:00–11:55 PM IST. The final cutoff is announced on Discord.
- **Free models:** a LiteLLM key, OpenAI-compatible, base `https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1`. Models: nova-micro/lite/pro, nova-2-lite, claude-haiku, claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-opus-4.6. $20 per team (https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/models).
- **Hackathon skill** (https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill): asks you to keep a `hackathon.md` at the repo root (project, stack, dated build log, evidence, limitations).

### 1. neatlogs
- **Docs:** full text at https://docs.neatlogs.com/llms-full.txt. SDKs: Python, TypeScript (Node ≥18), Go, Browser, plus HTTP `POST /v1/trace` and OTLP/gRPC `ingest.neatlogs.com:443` with header `x-api-key`.
- **TypeScript install:** `npm install neatlogs@latest`. The wizard is `npx @neatlogs/wizard@latest`.
- **Basic trace:**
```ts
import { init, wrapOpenAI, span, flush, shutdown } from 'neatlogs';
await init({ apiKey: process.env.NEATLOGS_API_KEY, workflowName: 'my-agent' });
const client = wrapOpenAI(new OpenAI({ baseURL: LITELLM_BASE, apiKey: process.env.LITELLM_API_KEY }));
const run = span({ kind: 'WORKFLOW' }, async (goal) => {...});
const tool = span({ kind: 'TOOL', toolName: 'search' }, async (q) => {...});
await flush(); await shutdown();   // short scripts lose traces without this
```
  - `init()` is async.
  - Wrap the entry point in a `WORKFLOW` span so all calls land in one trace.
  - Using `wrapOpenAI` with a custom `baseURL` (for LiteLLM) is my assumption; the docs don't show that case.
- **Explicit wrappers (TypeScript has no auto-instrumentation):**
  - `wrapAnthropic`
  - `wrapAISDK(ai)` from `neatlogs/ai` (AI SDK v6/v7; v7 needs Node 22+)
  - `wrapClaudeAgentSDK` from `neatlogs/claude-agent-sdk`
  - `wrapMastra`
  - `openaiAgentsProcessor()`
  - `langchainHandler()`
  - Python additionally has `neatlogs.wrap(...)` and LiteLLM support (`pip install "neatlogs[litellm]"`).
- **Sessions:** `identify({ sessionId, endUserId }, fn)`.
- **Claude Code tracing:** `npm i -g @neatlogs/claude-code && neatlogs-claude-code setup --global --api-key KEY`. This registers hooks and turns each Claude Code session into a trace.
- **MCP:** yes, Claude Code can read traces. Run `npx @neatlogs/wizard mcp --api-key KEY`, or add this to `.mcp.json`: `{"neatlogs":{"type":"http","url":"https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer KEY"}}}`.
  - Tools: `search_traces`, `get_trace_context`, `list_detections`, `get_detection_trend`, `triage_*` (fixes and investigations), `log_trace`, `whoami`.
- **Product features:** Investigate (Neat AI, Fast and Pro modes), Detections, Fixes, Evals (human or AI judges), Experiments (prompt versions plus Playground). The Datasets part of Experiments is "coming soon".
- **Not verified:** how to make a trace link public. The Public API has `GET /api/v1/public/traces/{id}/sharing` and the CLI has `neatlogs sharing traces get`, but I found no documented public-link toggle. Plan on screenshots plus dashboard URLs, and ask on Discord.
- **"Compare runs":** no dedicated docs page. The local tool neatroots (github.com/neatlogs/neatroots) offers "compare runs" through MCP.
- **Free tier:** 100k spans a month (hard cap), 3 investigations a month, 5 detectors, 2 users, 1 project, 14-day retention. Winners get 3 months of Pro.

### 2. Entire (https://docs.entire.io/llms-full.txt)
- **What it is:** Git hosting plus agent session capture. It was founded by the former GitHub CEO. The CLI is open source (MIT) at github.com/entireio/cli, latest v0.11.4, with darwin arm64 and amd64 builds.
- **Install without brew:** `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`. I read the script; it supports darwin and installs `entire` and `git-remote-entire` into `~/.local/bin`.
- **Setup in the repo:** `entire enable -y --agent claude-code`. This writes Claude Code hooks to `.claude/settings.json` and creates `.entire/settings.json`.
- **How a checkpoint is made:** on commit, Entire asks "Link this commit to session context? [Y/n/a]". Answer `a` (always) so Claude-made commits link automatically. The commit then gets an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer, and the transcript, tool calls, tokens, subagents and attribution are stored.
- **Storage:**
  - Default since 0.10.0 is ref-based: `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<ULID>`. GitHub's UI does not show these refs.
  - The branch backend stores everything on `entire/checkpoints/v1` with 12-hex IDs.
- **Use the branch backend:** `entire enable --checkpoint-backend branch` (or `entire configure --checkpoint-backend branch`).
  - **The judges' tool expects it:** entireio/entire-judge `add` fetches only `refs/heads/entire/*`, and its trailer regex matches only 12-hex IDs.
  - **Caveat:** I didn't confirm whether its `brain refresh` step fetches ref-based checkpoints on its own.
  - The branch is also visible on GitHub, and checkpoints show at `https://entire.io/gh/<org>/<repo>/commit/<sha>`. That view may need `entire login` plus the GitHub App.
- **entire-graph:** a plugin that maps code relationships for agents (claims up to 71% token savings).
  - Install with `entire plugin install graph`, check with `entire graph version`.
  - Run `entire graph init-agents --repo .`. This writes `.entire/graph-agent.md` and a managed block in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. Commit them.
  - Then prompt the agent, for example "Use entire-graph to find…". Needs git ≥2.36.
  - Also available: `entire mcp` (stdio MCP server), Brain, Search, Dispatches (shareable markdown summary of agent work).
- **Judge tool (github.com/entireio/entire-judge):** worth designing around. It scores:
  - authenticity (whether sessions began after the event started)
  - prompting_skill
  - idea/plan/execution (uses entire-graph data if present)
  - integrity (red flag when the team ignored warnings from the coding agent)
  - effort_consistency (rewards multiple sessions over one burst)
  - cli_awareness (rewards using `entire graph`, `entire brain` and Entire skills inside sessions)
- **Kickoff advice from Entire's judge:** "simple but elegant", and use Entire well. A previous winner built an Obsidian-style visual on entire-graph. PRs to Entire are a nice-to-have.

### 3. cfo.ai
- **What it is:** "Ari", an AI CFO. It builds a live financial model (Pages, Tables, Variables, Scenarios) from your data or from chat. Price: $500/mo after a 14-day trial.
- **Hackathon signup:** at cfo.ai/neathacks a card is required; cancel right away in Settings → Billing. The neatHack team supplies credits. The user has to do this step.
- **Outputs:**
  - Share → External link: read-only, no sign-in needed, optional password, choose which Scenario it shows. One link can cover several Pages. This is the judge link.
  - "Download spreadsheet" on any Page with tables (xlsx with live formulas). Ari can also export several Pages into one workbook.
- **MCP (verified):** `claude mcp add --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`, then `/mcp` → Authenticate in the browser.
  - Tools include `list_orgs`, `inspect_skills` (read the `build-model` skill), `inspect_pages`, `inspect_table_blocks`, `edit_table_blocks`, `edit_pages`, `edit_scenarios`, `edit_canvas_blocks`.
